searchText: Sure, yes, between the JSON approaches, definitely the CL REST-type is better here. It also transfers more naturally to the VC <-> BN communication, of course That said, I'm not convinced this flexibility or runtime mutability is much of a real advantage -- it creates an environment where it's appealing to, say, start treating some field as optional even though it's semantic nonsense, or avoid creating a new call or properly treating a response JSON type as distinct even when it definitely is, and to just push that back to some implicit disambiguation done at JSON parsing time (pre-Altair eth2 had some problems here, mostly fixed). The very up-front rigidity of SSZ can be advantageous in that regard, in making it clear that if one wants to return anything that's not an exact 1:1 mapping of the underlying SSZ type (which also can't randomly change), then one needs to define a new RPC method. Another general item that came up during discussions in DevConnect was that it'd be useful to have, like the engine API, some test of test vectors, for example some curl commands as a working reference for what a particular API looks like. sure, we'll have a couple example commands, and a simple test-program (because of the request signing). Just need the spec finalized. 🔥 I guess you mean SignedValidatorRegistration/ValidatorRegistration here in this line: https://github.com/lightclient/builder-apis/blob/main/apis/builder/validators.yaml#L8 what domain are we using to sign the validator registration (any tentative one?) `[10, 0, 0, 0]` lets say? https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2884
